subject: 2401 as a second household: a retired couple's home on the upper floor, and the garage level rented to a furniture maker as her workshop
notes: Two scenes on the same 12.1 x 8.5 m footprint as the reference environment, fitted to the same front windows (x -5.2, -1.4, +2.15, +5.3) and the same side-stair front door, but replanned for two people: a kitchen peninsula they actually eat at, a quilting room, a level-entry bath with grab bars, and a guest room doubling as a ham shack. Everything the catalog lacks is composed inline from boxes and cylinders; no prop was generated and nothing is embedded, so both models are self-contained. What reads: the shop is unmistakably a furniture shop from the clamp wall, the glue-up on sawhorses and the bench in the open, and the taped yellow walkway from the fourth door to the landlord's washer explains the whole landlord-tenant arrangement in one object; upstairs the puzzle left on the dining table, the two stools at the peninsula, the quilt on its frame and the shower with no tub read the household without labels. What does not: the new sill markers only hint at the front windows and the back rooms have none at all, because the exterior model carries windows on the street face only; thin things (the cane, the shower riser, clamp bars, hand tools) are lines from this height; the dust curtain reads as two bundles on a rail rather than as cloth; and with the walls cut at 0.8 m neither still shows sky.
